message:
Manager, Solar Energy Systems Engineer, Enclosure and Structural Designer, Smallholder Cooperative Operations Specialist, I close the thermal to electrical chain on a single stated basis.

In plain words cold heat is not wire electricity until divided by conversion efficiency. Reusing conduction 203 W from the conduction watts at 43C ambient 5C room (E41), staged pull-down 6.25 kilowatt-hour (kWh, energy) from the recompute sensible pull-down because E12 looks off by units (E26) under the staged rule from the revised steady load with 120mm PU and staged loading pull-down (E28), and respiration 1.20 kWh per day for mixed tomatoes and mangoes near 5 degrees Celsius from the Tahun 2000. Part IV processing by the removal of heat (E105), my single thermal total is conduction 4.87 plus respiration 1.20 plus door 0.17 plus staged pull-down 6.25 equals 12.5 kWh thermal per day, which supersedes the inconsistent 13.2 kWh per day from the steady plus staged pull-down daily kWh (E58) and the 12.8 kWh thermal per day from the thermal cooling total kWh_th per day conduction plus respiration plus door plus staged pull-down (E92). My single door model is 8 curtain openings per day with sensible plus latent from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) at 0.17 kWh per day, which supersedes 0.44 kWh per day sensible-only from the door infiltration kWh per day for 4 air changes (E57). Divided by Coefficient of Performance (COP, cooling per electric power) 1.40 for R134a BD50F-class at 43 degrees Celsius ambient plus fans 0.96 plus controls 0.48 equals 10.4 kWh electrical per day from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111). About one household daily use so everyday scale holds, and yield 13.5 kWh per day leaves about 3.1 kWh margin.

In plain words the box and refrigerant choices make that load attainable and serviceable. The box must achieve 200 W transmission ceiling at 38 Kelvin lift, with sealed rear penetration and shaded condenser, and R134a (refrigerant, A1 non-flammable) is chosen over R290 (propane refrigerant, A3 flammable) for village gauges and spares from the R134a vs. R290 Refrigerant: Key Differences & Replacements (E17), with hot operation allowed by evaporating range minus 30 to 0 degrees Celsius and maximum condensing 60 degrees Celsius from the BD50F Direct Current Compressor R134a, 12-24V DC & 100-240V AC 50/60Hz (E102), extreme 55 degrees Celsius condensing rating from the MAKING MODERN LIVING POSSIBLE (E112), and household COP basis from the | BD50F | (E98) derated to 1.40 hot. High rear evaporator to front airflow needs built hardware to prove uniformity and 43 degrees Celsius pull-down timing, named as bench test, not proven here.

My position is not ready on the proposal as a whole, because the proposal still states 13.2 kWh load with 0.30 kWh margin which my 10.4 kWh electrical total from the reconciled electrical total with curtain latent door model (E111) and 0.17 kWh door model from the single door model 8 curtain openings sensible plus latent (E110) supersede, pending Manager update and joint confirmation with Solar Energy Systems Engineer and Enclosure and Structural Designer.
